notes.meaning: The surviving military leaders and all the people gathered together and came to Jeremiah. After the governor was murdered, the entire group was terrified and looking for safety. Leaders and ordinary citizens alike joined together to seek guidance from God's prophet.

The leaders humbly asked Jeremiah to pray to the Lord for the small group that remained. They pointed out that only a few of them were left after wars and disasters had wiped out the rest of the nation. They spoke with great respect, presenting themselves as helpless survivors in desperate need of divine help.

The people asked Jeremiah to find out where they should go and what they should do next. Their hearts were already leaning toward fleeing to Egypt, but they wanted God to give His blessing to their travel plans. Genuine prayer seeks to discover God's will rather than asking Him to rubber-stamp our own choices.

Jeremiah agreed to bring their request before the Lord in prayer. He reminded them that the Lord was their God as well as his, so they had a duty to listen to Him. He promised to hold nothing back and to tell them everything God said, whether it was easy to hear or not.

The people made a solemn oath, calling on the Lord to be a witness against them if they failed to follow His commands. By calling God as their witness, they agreed that He had every right to punish them if they broke their word. They wanted Jeremiah to believe they were completely dedicated to doing whatever God required.

The people promised to obey God whether His instructions felt pleasant or unpleasant. They recognized the basic truth of the covenant that things go well for God's people only when they listen to His voice. True obedience means following God even when His commands go against our personal preferences.

God did not speak right away, but waited ten days before giving Jeremiah the answer. This delay proved that Jeremiah could not invent prophecies on the spot, but had to wait for God's timing. It also tested the people's patience and gave them time to think quietly about their promise.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some nineteenth-century critical scholars argued that Jeremiah took ten days to think through the political situation on his own and gather news before deciding what to say.

notes.meaning: As soon as the message came, Jeremiah called together Johanan, the army commanders, and all the people. No one was left out, from the most powerful leader to the humblest citizen. Because the whole community had asked the question, the whole community needed to hear the answer.

Jeremiah opened his speech by reminding the crowd that he was speaking for the Lord, the God of Israel. He pointed out that they were the very ones who had sent him to present their plea before God. Because they had asked for God's word, they were fully responsible to obey it.

God promised that if the people stayed in Judah, He would establish them safely, building them up like a house and planting them like a tree. He said He relented of the disaster, meaning the heavy season of judgment on their nation was finished and He was now ready to show them mercy. God was willing to bless them right where they were if they simply trusted Him.

The Lord told the people not to dread the king of Babylon, even though they feared he would punish them for Gedaliah's murder. God assured them of His personal presence to protect and deliver them from the Babylonian army. When God promises to protect His people, human rulers lose their power to harm them.

God promised to treat the people with mercy and to move the heart of the Babylonian king to show them kindness as well. Instead of executing revenge, the king would allow them to live in peace and work their own fields and vineyards. God has the power to change the hearts of foreign rulers to care for His people.

Jeremiah laid out the alternative choice: refusing to stay in the land was direct rebellion against God. The people longed for Egypt because they imagined it was free from war, alarm trumpets, and food shortages. They made the tragic mistake of looking for peace in an idolatrous land instead of trusting God's promise of safety at home.

Jeremiah gave a direct and solemn warning to the remaining survivors of Judah. The Lord of hosts, the all-powerful ruler of armies, spoke directly to their secret intentions. If they remained stubbornly determined to pack up and settle in Egypt, severe trouble would follow them.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some critical commentators suggest verses 15 through 18 were added later by an editor rather than spoken originally by Jeremiah.

notes.meaning: The very things the people ran away from—the sword of war and the pain of starvation—would track them down in Egypt. Nebuchadnezzar's forces would eventually invade Egypt, leaving the refugees trapped in the disaster they tried to avoid. Running away from God's path only leads directly into the dangers we dread most.

Everyone who stubbornly chose to settle in Egypt would fall by war, hunger, or terrible disease. Not a single person among those who defied God's command would survive the coming judgment. Refusing to trust God's protection always turns out to be a fatal decision.

God warned that His anger would be poured out on them in Egypt just as it had been poured out on Jerusalem during the siege. They would become a shocking sight, an insult, and a byword to other nations, and they would never see their homeland again. Having witnessed Jerusalem fall, they should have known that God's warnings always come true.

Jeremiah made the message crystal clear: the Lord commanded the survivors not to cross the border into Egypt. The prophet reminded them that he was giving a formal and public warning right to their faces. Because they were warned so clearly, they could never claim ignorance if disaster struck them.

Jeremiah exposed the deceit in their hearts when they sent him to pray for guidance. While they used spiritual language and promised to obey whatever God said, they had already made up their minds to run to Egypt. Playing religious games and pretending to seek God's will only brings harm to one's own soul.

Jeremiah explained that he had faithfully delivered everything God commanded, yet he already knew they refused to listen. Their faces and stubborn attitudes showed that they disliked God's answer and would not obey it. The prophet had done his complete duty, leaving the people entirely accountable for their rebellion.

Jeremiah finished his message with an absolute certainty: they would die by violence, hunger, and disease in Egypt. The very country where they hoped to find a safe home would become their graveyard. Disobeying God to chase worldly safety always ends in ruin.
